title: Bundled GitHub.copilot-chat throws "CANNOT use API proposal: envIsConnectionMetered" on every inline completion request
body:
### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

Yes. `GitHub.copilot-chat` is the bundled extension (`resources/app/extensions/copilot`),
so this reproduces with every user-installed extension disabled. No marketplace copy
of the extension is installed.

### Summary

Every automatic inline completion request makes the bundled `GitHub.copilot-chat` throw:

```
Error: Extension 'GitHub.copilot-chat' CANNOT use API proposal: envIsConnectionMetered.
```

`product.json`'s `extensionEnabledApiProposals` grant for `GitHub.copilot-chat` is out
of sync with the extension's own manifest. The extension declares
`envIsConnectionMetered`; the product override does not. The result is that Copilot
inline completions do not work at all on this build, silently, with no UI surface.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch VS Code Insiders with all extensions disabled.
2. Open any file and type for a few seconds.
3. Inspect `~/.config/Code - Insiders/logs/<session>/window1/exthost/exthost.log`
   (Output panel → "Extension Host" shows the same content).

One exception per debounced automatic completion request.

### Actual error (verbatim, single occurrence)

```
2026-09-10 13:32:20.441 [error] Error: Extension 'GitHub.copilot-chat' CANNOT use API proposal: envIsConnectionMetered.
Its package.json#enabledApiProposals-property declares: agentSessionsWorkspace, agentsWindowConfiguration, interactive, terminalDataWriteEvent, termin..., but NOT envIsConnectionMetered.
The missing proposal MUST be added and you must start in extension development mode or use the following command line switch: --enable-proposed-api GitHub.copilot-chat
    at M (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:518:1689)
    at Object.get isMeteredConnection [as isMeteredConnection] (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:672:140185)
    at Ame.provideInlineCompletionItems (/usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:5086:3109)
    at is.provideInlineCompletions (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:582:154324)
    at file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:582:180349
    at r._withAdapter (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:582:167792)
    at r.$provideInlineCompletions (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:582:180326)
    at r._doInvokeHandler (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:435:159637)
    at r._invokeHandler (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:435:159385)
    at r._receiveRequest (file:///usr/share/code-insiders/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:435:158074)
```

### Root cause

The grant is resolved from `product.json`, not from the extension's own manifest.
Evidence: the proposal list printed in the error is identical to
`product.json`'s `extensionEnabledApiProposals["GitHub.copilot-chat"]` array —
verified by diffing the two sorted sets. It is *not* what the shipped extension's
`package.json` declares.

| Source | Entries | Includes `envIsConnectionMetered`? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resources/app/extensions/copilot/package.json` → `enabledApiProposals` | 64 | **yes** |
| `resources/app/product.json` → `extensionEnabledApiProposals["GitHub.copilot-chat"]` | 66 | **no** |

Symmetric difference between the two lists:

- only in `product.json`: `contribCommentEditorActionsMenu`, `extensionAffinity`, `tokenInformation`
- only in `package.json`: `envIsConnectionMetered`

The extension shipped in this build was therefore built against a proposal that the
`product.json` shipped in the same build does not grant.

### Why it fires on every keystroke

`extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js` calls `env.isMeteredConnection` at exactly two
places:

- line 5086, col 3109 — `CopilotInlineCompletionItemProvider.provideInlineCompletionItems`
- line 5300, col 21256 — the Next Edit Suggestions provider

At line 5086 the call is the **first operand** of the guard:

```js
async provideInlineCompletionItems(n, r, o, a) {
  if (o.triggerKind === InlineCompletionTriggerKind.Automatic && env.isMeteredConnection
   || o.triggerKind === InlineCompletionTriggerKind.Automatic
      && (!this.instantiationService.invokeFunction(eVt, n) || this.extensionStatusService.kind === "Error")) return;
  ...
}
```

`&&` short-circuits, so an `Automatic` trigger (as-you-type) always evaluates
`env.isMeteredConnection`, and its getter throws. The entitlement/language checks in
the second operand are never reached, and neither is the `github.copilot.enable`
enablement lookup (implemented in a separate helper) — so no user setting can
suppress this. I verified that `github.copilot.enable: { "*": false }` does not
stop it.

### Impact

- One thrown exception per debounced automatic completion request. Bursts of 6 in
  0.65 s observed while typing.
- 3,389 exceptions in a single session; ~15,000 across recent sessions.
- `exthost.log` rotates at 5 MB repeatedly (~35 MB of log per session), and each
  record embeds the full ~2,000-character proposal list.
- Copilot code completions are completely non-functional on this build, with the
  failure swallowed by the extension host. Possibly the same root cause as the
  closed #335351.

### VS Code version

```
Version: 1.138.0-insider
Commit: 1410ae566a7ec09ae775a65a995076f0e303fafb
Date: 2026-09-10T11:30:40+01:00
Electron: 42.10.0
ElectronBuildId: 15109253
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.1
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.84-3
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.13
OS: Linux x64 7.1.5-76070105-generic
```

Bundled extension: `GitHub.copilot-chat` v0.66.2026091004
(`extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js`, mtime 2026-09-10 04:44).

### Suggested fix

Add `"envIsConnectionMetered"` to
`extensionEnabledApiProposals["GitHub.copilot-chat"]` in `product.json` for every
build that ships this extension version. The proposal already exists in the core
(`extensionHostProcess.js` defines the `isMeteredConnection` env getter), so the
grant is the only missing piece.

### Workaround

`--enable-proposed-api GitHub.copilot-chat` (the switch named in the error message),
or locally adding the missing entry to `product.json`. Neither is a proper fix, and
the latter is overwritten by every update.

### Related

- #334669 — agentHost: Require explicit SDK download on metered connections (the
  feature that motivates the `env.isMeteredConnection` call)
- #335351 — Copilot code suggestions broken after update (closed)

This test covers the Preview settings that opt agent sessions with merged pull requests into automatic archival and later permanent deletion. Note this requires testing for over a day.

For this lifecycle, a session is **inactive** when it is not currently in progress and its provider-reported last-modified time is at least the configured number of days old. The separate deletion grace period starts when the lifecycle automatically archives the session, not at the session's last-modified time.

## Setup

- Use Insiders with an Agent Host harness and the Agents Window enabled.
- Use disposable sessions and repositories. Permanent deletion cannot be undone.
- Have:
  - an inactive session with at least one merged pull request and no open related pull requests;
  - a session with an open related pull request;
  - a manually archived session;
  - if practical, both a clean worktree that tracks an upstream and a worktree with uncommitted or outgoing changes.

## Verify the settings

- Open Settings and search for `archive`.
- Verify exactly these two application-scoped Preview settings are shown:
  - `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
- Verify both default to `0`, explain that zero disables the behavior, recommend 15 days, and link to each other.
- Verify the archive setting describes inactivity before archival and safe cleanup of eligible worktrees.
- Verify the delete setting describes a separate grace period after automatic archival, permanent deletion, and safe cleanup of retained eligible worktrees.
- Enter positive whole-number values and verify they are accepted. Verify negative and fractional values are rejected.
- Set both settings to `0` and reload VS Code. Verify existing sessions are neither automatically archived nor deleted.
- Set only the archive setting to a positive value and verify permanent deletion remains disabled.
- Set only the delete setting to a positive value and verify startup/hourly lifecycle evaluation remains enabled, but sessions that were not automatically archived are not made deletion-eligible.
- If the **Configure Automatic Cleanup** or **Open Settings** action is available from a merged-PR session suggestion, activate it and verify Settings opens filtered to only these two settings.

title: Make tokenization registries and token palettes scopeable for multi-theme fixtures
body:
## Engineering task

Make editor tokenization registries and token palettes scopeable/injectable so multiple differently themed editor fixtures can coexist in **one JavaScript context** while using VS Code's real TextMate implementation.

This is a future infrastructure task, separate from the multi-diff styling and fixture work that motivated it. Iframe isolation is not a solution for this use case.

## Motivation

Component fixtures need to render Dark, Light, and high-contrast editors together. TextMate's encoded tokens contain palette indices, but editor models and several renderers currently use the process-wide `TokenizationRegistry` and its color map. Switching that global theme per fixture cannot reliably preserve the relationship between each model's tokens and its palette.

Reusing `TMGrammarFactory`, `TextMateTokenizationSupport`, the shipped grammars, and Oniguruma should not require approximating syntax scopes or changing fixture model language IDs. WASM/grammar initialization can be asynchronous; tokenization itself can remain synchronous after initialization.

## Proposed direction

- Introduce explicit, injectable ownership for tokenization registries and token palettes. Preserve the existing default behavior for production consumers and standalone APIs.
- Allow fixture child instantiation scopes to own their registry, TextMate grammar factory, palette, and token CSS while sharing the WASM runtime and loaded grammar assets where appropriate.
- Thread the scope through text-model tokenization and editor rendering. A palette-only service is insufficient if model tokenization still uses another registry.
- Pass dependencies through the existing editor/view context where components are not directly constructed through DI.
- Make the minimap color tracker scope-owned rather than a process-wide singleton.
- Ensure registrations, listeners, factories, and caches have explicit disposal ownership.

Relevant starting points:
- `src/vs/editor/common/languages.ts`: existing `ITokenizationRegistry` contract and global instance.
- `src/vs/editor/common/tokenizationRegistry.ts`: registry and color-map storage.
- `src/vs/editor/common/model/tokens/tokenizerSyntaxTokenBackend.ts`: global tokenizer lookup/change subscription.
- `src/vs/editor/common/viewModel/minimapTokensColorTracker.ts`: global palette cache.
- `src/vs/editor/common/viewModel/viewContext.ts`: dependency propagation to view parts.
- `src/vs/workbench/services/textMate/browser/textMateTokenizationFeatureImpl.ts`: TextMate registration and palette publication.

## Audited palette consumers

In the motivating checkout, there are 18 files with 20 direct palette-read sites: 15 runtime files and 3 development/fixture files.

Runtime uses include:
- Minimap colors and overview-ruler background/change handling.
- Clipboard HTML, IME composition text, and token inspection.
- Token CSS for extensions, MCP/plugins, release notes, walkthroughs, notebooks, and mobile diffs.
- Notebook drag previews and extension-API syntax-highlighting results.

Also account for indirect minimap consumers and change-event-only consumers such as hover rerendering. The two production palette writers are `StandaloneThemeService` and `TextMateTokenizationFeature`; existing fixture writers need migration too.

## Acceptance criteria

- Dark, Light, and both high-contrast fixtures can render concurrently in one JS context with real TextMate tokenization and no cross-fixture palette interference.
- Original language IDs, grammar injections, token-type metadata, and language-feature behavior are preserved.
- Text, font styles, minimap/canvas rendering, clipboard/IME colors, and other palette-dependent paths use the matching scope.
- Changing or disposing one fixture's theme/registry does not retokenize, recolor, or break another fixture.
- Existing production and standalone behavior is preserved, including lazy tokenizer registration and palette-change notifications.
- Targeted tests cover simultaneous themes, differing render/disposal orders, updates, and leak-free teardown.

Semantic highlighting from language-service providers is a separate concern; it should not be conflated with TextMate syntax highlighting in this task.

title: Surface MCP authentication problems persistently in the primary UI
body:
## Summary

MCP authentication problems are effectively hidden until after I send a request that needs the affected server.

The primary **Customizations** UI shows counts for Plugins, MCP Servers, Skills, and other customization types, but gives no persistent indication that one or more MCP servers need authentication or are otherwise unavailable.

## Actual behavior

1. An MCP server's credentials expire or otherwise require authentication.
2. Open the Agents window and its **Customizations** UI.
3. There is no visible warning or unhealthy-server count on **Overview** or **MCP Servers**.
4. Send a request that depends on the affected server.
5. Only after sending, a short-lived authentication affordance appears for a few seconds. It is easy to miss or not complete in time.
6. The agent continues without that source/tool. Only later in the response does the capability gap become apparent, for example:

> **Source gap:** The Slack connector was unavailable, so I could not verify or cite the supporting Slack discussion.

At that point the request has already run and produced an incomplete answer.

## Expected behavior

MCP authentication and connection health should be visible persistently before a request is sent, with a durable recovery action. For example:

- Show an error/warning badge or unhealthy count on the **MCP Servers** row in Customizations.
- Show affected servers and their status on the Customizations Overview.
- Keep the warning visible until authentication succeeds or the server is disabled.
- Provide a reliable **Authenticate** / **Reconnect** action from that status.
- Consider a pre-send warning when the request/session expects tools from an unavailable MCP server, rather than silently continuing with reduced capabilities.

The important part is that this is not only a transient notification after submission. Authentication trouble should be discoverable from the primary UI at any time.

## Impact

- Users do not know an MCP-backed source is unavailable before asking a question.
- Requests run with silently reduced capabilities and return partial answers.
- The recovery window is brief and appears at the wrong time: after the user has already committed the request.
- This makes source-backed answers harder to trust because the missing capability is disclosed only later in the response.

## Related issues

- #327640 — Agent Sessions authentication action is a no-op and the flow has no feedback.
- #330837 — credential failures can remove MCP tools with no surfaced error or reset path.
- #334271 — interactive MCP activation failures leave tools absent with no surfaced error.

The existing reports cover broken authentication and silent tool loss. This issue is specifically about a persistent, proactive health signal and recovery entry point in the primary UI.

title: fix: raise telemetry-extractor heap limit to prevent build OOM (build fix for vscode-engineering#3836)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

body:
## Build failure

The `Generate lists of telemetry events` build task crashed with a V8 out-of-memory error while running `@vscode/telemetry-extractor`:

```
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

The crash occurred near ~2052 MB. The remaining failed tasks in the build (1ES verify + crash/log publish) were downstream cascades of the extractor never producing its output paths.

## Root cause

`build/azure-pipelines/common/extract-telemetry.ts` invokes the extractor with plain `node "${extractor}" ...` and no heap flag, so it runs at V8's default ~2 GB old-space limit. The extractor loads telemetry declarations for the whole `sourceDir` tree into memory; as the tree grows it deterministically crosses that ceiling. This is a resource ceiling rather than a specific regression — no commit in the build window touches telemetry extraction.

## How the fix works

Both `node` extractor invocations now pass `--max-old-space-size=8192`, raising the old-space heap to 8 GB and giving extraction headroom well above the previous ~2 GB crash point. The flag is defined once as `extractorNodeOptions` and applied to both calls, with a comment documenting why. No behavior changes beyond the heap limit; telemetry output and error reporting are unchanged.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Culprit commit/PR: `not confirmed` — the failure is a deterministic build-tool heap ceiling, and the product commits in the build window do not touch telemetry extraction, so there is no code regression to revert. A bounded heap bump lands quickly and safely; a rollback would not address the OOM. Owners to consult: `@joaomoreno`

## Validation

Source inspection only. The change is confined to two shell command strings in a build script; the extractor binary and arguments are otherwise unchanged. CI validation happens when the telemetry extraction task runs in the pipeline. Local build/pipeline validation of this task was not run with the available tools.

## Risk

Low. The only effect is a higher permitted heap for a short-lived build subprocess. No product code or runtime behavior is affected.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@joaomoreno`

title: Give IconLabel ownership of icon-label spacing
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Abandoned experiment.** The `IconLabel` audit was useful, but this implementation introduced a public option, runtime host tracking, consumer overrides, and extensive tests for a very small product effect. It is not part of the active proposal or stack. The retained conclusion is that `Button` already reuses `renderLabelWithIcons`, while the full `IconLabel` widget is a separate resource/list-label abstraction that does not need to change for #335350.

## Predictable UI composition - 4 of 4: `IconLabel` shared-control pilot

This is the fourth PR in the draft stack:

1. **#335345 - candidate token foundation:** register the proposed spacing and icon-size vocabulary.
2. **#335346 - candidate authoring guidance:** derive a property-agnostic ownership rule.
3. **#335350 - `WorkbenchButtonBar` pilot:** consolidate the button’s leading icon/spinner slot relationship.
4. **This PR - `IconLabel` pilot:** consolidate the shared resource/list-label icon relationship and migrate one production override.

This remains an experiment supporting #335354. It validates `IconLabel` as a second shared-control counterexample; it does not make every icon-label composition use this widget.

## Problem

`IconLabel` already owns the relationship between its leading icon and label, but its two rendering paths encoded the same geometry independently:

- file/product icon classes render through `::before` with a 16px width and 6px right padding;
- explicit `iconPath` values render a child node with a 16px width and 6px right margin.

Modern UI compact pinned tabs then removed both contributions with separate consumer selectors. The effective icon-only composition therefore depended on the consumer knowing both internal render paths.

## Pilot implementation

- Adds `IIconLabelValueOptions.iconLabelSpacing` with behavior-safe `default` and `none` variants. Omission preserves the existing 6px relationship.
- Gives both icon paths the shared `--vscode-iconSize-small` role. Relationship spacing uses `margin-inline-end`, keeping it outside the painted pseudo-element for RTL; predefined ThemeIcon optical padding stays inside a fixed 16px border-box. Every registered size variable retains its existing literal as a fallback for standalone Monaco.
- Keeps the explicit icon-path slot fixed while label text truncates.
- Threads the option through `ResourceLabel`.
- Makes `MultiEditorTabsControl` select `none` for compact pinned icon-only tabs from the actual `.modern-ui-tabs` composition signal (or the Sessions constructor flag), refreshes labels when that runtime signal changes during layout, and removes the two path-specific consumer overrides.
- Leaves ordinary labels, classic tabs, inline `$(icon)` segments, descriptions, hover behavior, and accessible names unchanged.

The full `IconLabel` widget is still not used inside `Button`; both controls already share the lower-level `renderLabelWithIcons` helper, while their leading-slot semantics remain distinct.

## Review findings addressed

- **Standalone Monaco:** every new size-variable use now carries the existing literal as its fallback, and a browser test masks the variables to verify both icon paths retain 16px/6px default geometry.
- **Blocking visual coverage:** both the shared `IconLabel` fixture and the Modern UI compact-pinned-tab fixture now set `blocksCi: true`; the rendered manifest confirms their `blocks-ci` label.
- **Modern UI host signal:** compact-tab spacing now follows the runtime `.modern-ui-tabs` ancestor used by regular workbench sizing as well as the Sessions constructor flag. Layout detects signal changes and redraws label variants; a unit test covers default → none → default transitions, and the production fixture throws unless it reaches the `none` branch.
- **ThemeIcon, RTL, and existing consumers:** pseudo-element relationship spacing moved to logical margin, predefined ThemeIcon fitting is contained within the fixed icon box, and a computed browser test covers the real higher-specificity workbench rule. Single-editor breadcrumbs and workbench/Sessions attachment labels explicitly retain their existing 2px/4px consumer-owned spacing without stacking the new margin.

## Validation evidence

Two blocking `base/iconLabel` fixtures cover the pseudo-element path, explicit `iconPath`, inline label icons, the `none` variant, truncation, descriptions, and a non-default 20px token override across predefined ThemeIcon and explicit paths. The existing production-derived compact-pinned-tab fixture is now blocking for Modern UI and exercises the real `MultiEditorTabsControl` selection.

Both fixtures render in dark and light themes without errors. After rebasing onto latest `origin/main`, a 542-fixture comparison found 534 pixel-identical fixtures. The only tab changes are dark/light compact pinned tabs in single- and separate-row layouts, directly related to #331234; the representative delta is 67 pixels across three icon glyphs. Ordinary, single, and no-icon tabs remain unchanged.

### Measured shared contract

| Rendering path | Variant / override | Computed icon slot | Computed gap | Label start in fixture |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| File-theme pseudo-element | `default` | 16px | 6px | 194px |
| Explicit `iconPath` | `default` | 16px | 6px | 194px |
| Explicit `iconPath` | `none` | 16px | 0px | 188px |
| Predefined ThemeIcon pseudo-element | 20px token override | 20px | 6px | 198px |
| Explicit ThemeIcon `iconPath` | 20px token override | 20px | 6px | 198px |

The x-coordinates are fixture-local measurements, not design values. They show that equivalent paths align and that only the selected relationship changes. The raw contract fixtures remain CI-blocking but are omitted here because mixing file-theme and Codicon artwork is poor visual evidence for geometry; the computed measurements and dedicated path tests are more precise.

### Production behavior: compact pinned tabs

| Concern | Current — Latest Main | Proposed — This Stack |
|---|---|---|
| Icon-only relationship | Modern UI CSS separately resets pseudo-element padding and `iconPath` margin | `MultiEditorTabsControl` selects the `none` relationship once |
| Predefined ThemeIcon fitting | Optical padding participates in the pseudo-element’s content-box footprint | Optical padding is contained inside the shared 16px border-box |
| Explicit `iconPath` fitting | Separate path-specific margin reset | Same `none` contract as the pseudo-element path |
| Tab bounds | 28px compact tab | Unchanged |
| Labelled and no-icon tabs | Existing behavior | Unchanged |

The stable 542-fixture comparison found changes only in compact pinned tabs and the intentionally expanded button fixtures; 534 related fixtures were pixel-identical. The compact-tab raster delta is just 67 anti-aliased edge pixels across three glyphs, which is below a useful human-review threshold at native scale, so it is intentionally **not** shown as visual proof. The CI-blocking production fixture and computed geometry tests are the authoritative evidence for this path.

## Automated validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/browser/iconLabels.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` - 16 tests pass
- Stylelint across all eight affected CSS files - clean (existing advisory suggestions are outside the changed declarations)
- Editor diagnostics on all changed TypeScript files - clean
- `git diff --check` - clean

## Review questions

- Is `none` plus compatibility-preserving `default` the right initial contract for this shared component?
- Is Modern UI compact pinned tabs the right first production migration, given that the label is intentionally absent there?
- Does keeping the two CSS mechanisms but moving variant selection into `IconLabel` express ownership clearly enough without exposing a component-local CSS variable?

## Context

- **Umbrella proposal:** #335354
- **Token foundation:** #335345
- **Authoring guidance:** #335346
- **First shared-control pilot:** #335350
- **Originating report:** #331234
